title: Base-dense rational maps and maximal domains
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. An open $U\subseteq X$ is base-dense if its inverse image in every scheme-theoretic fibre is dense [def-pc-base-change]. For the smooth separated trait models [def-sfb-smooth-trait-model], a base-rational map is an ordinary rational map which has a representative on a base-dense open, with representative map over $S$. Equivalently its representatives are identified by agreement on a base-dense common open. Its maximal representative has domain the union of all representative domains and is over $S$. A generic isomorphism is an isomorphism of the specified common generic fibre whose composite with the target inclusion agrees with a representative after lifting the source generic inclusion through that representative domain. Birational over $S$ means represented by an isomorphism of base-dense open subschemes.
